questions.question: What is the sum of all prime numbers between 60 and 80?
questions.solution:
Prime numbers between 60 and 80 are 61, 67, 71, 73, and 79

Their sum can be written as 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 = 351

∴ The sum of all prime numbers between 60 and 80 is 351

questions.question: A and B have to type a book together containing 120 pages. A takes 9 hrs to type 36 pages and B takes 5 hrs to type 40 pages. A typed first 60 pages alone and the last 60 pages were typed by A and B together. How much time (in hours) will be taken to type the complete book?
questions.solution:
Number of pages typed by A in 1 hour = 36/9 = 4 pages per hour

Number of pages typed by B in 1 hour = 40/5 = 8 pages per hour

According to the problem statement

Time required by A to type 6o pages = 60/4 = 15 hours

When they work together their speed = 4 + 8 = 12 pages per hour

Now Time required to type remaining 60 pages = 60/12 = 5 hours

Total time required = 15 hours + 5 hours = 20 hours

∴ Time required is 20 hours

questions.question: ABC is a right angled triangle in which ∠B = 90°, AB = 5 cm and BC = 12 cm. What is the approximate volume (in cm³) of the double cone formed by rotating the triangle about its hypotenuse?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

ABC is a right angled triangle in which ∠B = 90°, AB = 5 cm and BC = 12 cm.

**Formula used:**

Pythagoras theorem

Volume of cone = (1/3)π r² h

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c4a86b59a9b57eab52286be90477370356d893745da71c84f28bff34300bdd3.png] 

Applying Pythagoras theorem in triangle ABC

AC² = BC² + AB²

⇒ AC = √(12² + 5²) = √169

⇒ AC = 13 cm

Area of triangle ABC = (1/2) × AB × BC = (1/2) × AC × OB

⇒ OB × 13 = 5 × 12

⇒ OB = 60/13 cm 

Volume of double cone = Volume of cone1 + Volume of cone2

⇒ (1/3) π r² h₁ + (1/3) π r² h₂

⇒ (1/3)× 3.14 × OB² × (OA + OC)

⇒ (1/3)× 3.14 × (60/13)² × 13

⇒ 11304/39 = 289.85

⇒ 290 cm³.

**∴ The volume of double cone is 290 cm³**.

questions.question: A trader allowed a discount of 15% on a trolley bag having list price of Rs 1360 and earns a profit of 15.6%. What is the cost price (in Rs) of the trolley bag?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price be Rs. y

Selling price of article = 15% discount on 1360 = 1360 × (1 - 15/100) = 0.85 × 1360 = Rs. 1156

Profit of 15.6% can be written as

⇒ y(1 + 15.6/100) = 1.156 y = Rs. 1156

⇒ 1.156y = 1156

⇒ y = 1000

∴ The cost price is Rs. 1000

questions.question: Price of a diamond is directly proportional to square of its weight. A man broke the diamond accidently in three pieces in the ratio of 3 : 5 : 7 and thus loses Rs 42600. What was the original price (in Rs) of the diamond?
questions.solution:
Let total weight of the diamond is 15 gm.

So, Original price of the diamond = k × 15² = Rs. 225k

Diamond is broken into 3 parts in the ratio of 3 : 5 : 7

Therefore weights of the pieces are 3 gm, 5 gm and 7 gm respectively

Let value of the pieces be Rs. 9k, Rs. 25k, Rs. 49k respectively

According to the question,

225k – [9k + 25k + 49k] = 42600

⇒ 142k = 42600

⇒ k = 42600/142 = 300

∴ Original price of the diamond = 225k = 225 × 300 = Rs. 67500

questions.question: The average weight of 100 students is 32 kg. The average weight of first 49 students is 30 kg and of last 50 students is 34 kg. What is the weight (in kg) of the 50th student?
questions.solution:
According to the question

Sum of weight of all 100 students/100 = 32

Sum of weight of all 100 students = 3200

Now the average weight of first 49 students is 30 can be written as

Sum of weight of first 49 students/49 = 30

⇒ sum of weight of first 49 students = 30 × 49 = 1470

Given that the average weight of last 50 students is 34 can be written as

sum of weight of last 50 students/50 = 34

⇒ sum of weight of last 50 students = 34 × 50 = 1700

Weight of 50th student can be written as = sum of age of all students – sum of age of first 49 students – sum of last 50 students

⇒ Weight of 50th student can be written as = 3200 – 1470 – 1700 = 30

∴ The weight of 50th student is 30 Kg

questions.question: Raman spends 80% of his income. If his income is increased by 25% and the expenditure increase by 10%, then what will be the percentage increase in his savings?
questions.solution:
Let the income of Raman be Rs. 100

According to the problem statement

Amount to be spend by Raman can be given as

Amount spent = 100 × (80/100) = Rs. 80

Now the savings is 100 – 80 = Rs. 20

If income increased by 25%, new income will be

New income = 100 × (1 + 25/100) = Rs. 125

Expenditure increased by 10% can be given as

⇒ final expenditure = 80 × (1 + 10/100) = 80 × 1.1 = Rs. 88

Savings can be given as 125 – 88 = 37

Increase in saving is 37 – 20 = Rs. 17

⇒ percentage increase in savings can be given as = 17 × 100/20 = 85%

∴ The increase in savings is 85%

questions.question: A man makes four trips of equal distances. His speed on first trip was 60 km/hr and in each subsequent trip his speed was half of the previous trip. What is the average speed (in km/hr) of the man in these four trips?
questions.solution:
Let the distance of each trip be d

For first trip time can be given as

time for first trip = d/60

For second trip, since speed is now 30 km/hr time can be given as

time for second trip = d/30

For third trip, since speed is now 15 km/hr time can be given as

time for second trip = d/15

For fourth trip, since speed is now 7.5 km/hr time can be given as

time for second trip = d/7.5

Average Speed can be given as total distance travelled/total time taken

Average speed = 4d/{(d/60) + (d/30) + (d/15) + (d/7.5)}

⇒ Average speed = 240/15 = 16

∴ the average speed is 16 km/hr

questions.question: Rohan borrowed a certain sum of money at simple interest. Rate of interest was 3% per annum for first 3 years, 4% per annum for next 5 years and 6% per annum for next 7 years. If he paid Rs 2059 as interest, then what is the sum borrowed (in Rs)?
questions.solution:
Let the sum borrowed be Rs. Y

According to the problem statement

Total interest = (y × 3 × 3)/100 + ( y × 4 × 5)/100 + ( y × 6 × 7)/100

⇒ 2059 × 100 = 71y

⇒ y = 2900

∴ The sum borrowed is Rs. 2900

questions.question: If x + y = 5, x³ + y³ = 35, then what is the positive difference between x and y?
questions.solution:
From the given equation we can see that

⇒ x³ + y³ = 35 = 27 + 8 = 3³ + 2³

From this x = 3 and y = 2

This also satisfies x + y = 5

⇒ Positive difference between them is 3 - 2 = 1

∴ The difference between the numbers is 1

questions.question: If x = sqrt {frac{{2 + sqrt 3 }}{{2 - sqrt 3 }}}, then what is the value of (x² + x – 9)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x = √{(2 + √3)/(2 - √3)}

**Formula Used:**

(a + b) × (a – b) = a² – b² 

(a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2

**Calculation:**

x = √{(2 + √3)/(2 - √3)}

Rationalizing this

x = √{(2 + √3)²/(2 + √3) × (2 - √3)}

⇒ √{(2 + √3)²/(4 – 3)}

⇒ x = 2 + √3

Put this in the expression x² + x – 9

⇒ (2 + √3)² + (2 + √3) – 9

⇒ 4 + 3 + 4 √3 + 2 + √3 – 9

⇒ 5 √3

**∴ The value of given expression is 5√3.**

questions.question: If cot A = [sin B/(1 – cos B)], then what is the value of cot 2A?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cot A = [sin B/(1 – cos B)]

**Formula Used:**

**1**. sin2θ = 2 (sinθ × cosθ)

**2**. cos2θ = 1 - 2sin²θ

**Solution:**

Since we know that sin B = 2sin(B/2)cos(B/2)

And 1 – cos B = 2 sin²(B/2)

Put all these things in the required equation

⇒ cot A = (2sin(B/2)cos(B/2)) / ( 2 sin²(B/2))

⇒ cot A = cot (B/2)

⇒ cot (2A) = cot (2 × B/2)

⇒ cot (B)

**∴ The simplified value is cot(B).**

questions.question: Company 1 sold 20000 bikes each year from 2011 to 2016 and company 2 sold 10000 bikes each year from 2011 to 2016. What is the difference (in units) in average yearly production of company 1 and 2?
questions.solution:
For company 1 total production from year 2011 to 2016 can be given as

⇒ total production = sale per year × (sum of ratios of all year), because sale is same in all years

⇒ total production for company 1 = 20000 × (0.6 + 0.9 + 0.7 + 0.9 + 1.3 + 1.3)

⇒ total production = 114000

⇒ Average = 114000/6 = 19000

For company 2 total production from year 2011 to 2016 can be given as

⇒ total production = sale per year × (sum of ratios of all year), because sale is same in all years

⇒ total production for company 2 = 10000 × (0.8 + 0.75 + 0.4 + 1.45 + 1.3 + 1.1)

⇒ total production = 58000

⇒ Average = 58000/6 = 9666.66

⇒ Difference is 19000 – 9666.66

∴ The difference is 9333.34
